sample.question.sensor.body:
I use a DS18B20 sensor to monitor the temperature of an industrial oven in a small factory, but readings fluctuate wildly (±4 degrees) whenever the motor near the sensor runs.

I tried a simple moving average and it helped a little, but I don't know whether the problem is in the code or in the electrical wiring. Here is part of my current code:
sample.answer.isolation: Most likely it's the isolation, not the code: use a shielded cable, connect its shield to ground at one end only, and add a 100nF capacitor near the sensor. After that, a simple Kalman filter is enough to smooth the readings.
sample.answer.median: Before changing the wiring, try taking several samples each cycle and discarding outliers (median filter), then average. This reduces the effect of momentary spikes caused by the motor running.
sample.problem.description: Our company runs a production line built around an industrial oven, and temperature readings fluctuate wildly when nearby motors run, causing false alarms and unnecessary stops. We're looking for a simple, low-cost system that reads temperature accurately and sends an alert when the limit is exceeded.
sample.problem.accuracy: Read temperature with at least ±0.5° accuracy
sample.problem.alert: Send an alert by email or SMS when the limit is exceeded
sample.problem.dashboard: A simple web dashboard showing the last 24 hours of readings
sample.problem.documentation: Short documentation on installation and calibration
sample.problem.budget: Hardware budget must not exceed 15,000 DZD
sample.problem.hardware: Runs on an ESP32 or equivalent
sample.problem.delivery: Delivery within 14 days of solution acceptance
sample.comment.visit: Can we visit the site to inspect the oven before submitting a solution?
sample.comment.arrange: Yes, we can arrange one visit per provisionally accepted proposal. We'll share the location after the initial review.
sample.comment.limit: Is there a limit on how many sensors can be installed in the oven?
sample.comment.points: The oven has three measurement points, and two more can be added if needed.
